subtype: Approach: telling the younger one to wait forever [Pitfall]
passage: In the small flat in Osaka, Hiroshi held the game controller and did not look up. "Big brother, can I have a turn?" Esther asked. "Later," said Hiroshi. An hour passed. "Now?" "Later." Another hour. Esther sat with her chin on the sofa arm, watching the screen without playing. At six she stood up, walked to the kitchen and said quietly to her mother, "Hiroshi says later, but it never comes." Mama put down the knife. She had to stop dinner, come into the living room, and take the controller herself to sort out whose turn it was. Hiroshi complained. Esther said nothing, but she looked tired.

qa.q: Where did Esther go at six o'clock?
qa.a: Esther went to the kitchen to talk to her mother.

qa.q: What was Esther feeling as she sat watching without playing?
qa.a: Esther felt ignored and disappointed, since 'later' never came and she was left watching. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Hiroshi use, and why?
qa.a: Hiroshi could say when the turn starts, such as after this level, and keep the promise. A clear time lets Esther trust that the wait will end.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Mama?
qa.a: Mama had to stop cooking to settle a turn between two children, so Mama probably feels interrupted and wishes they had agreed on it alone.

grounding: An elder brother tells his little sister she can have a turn later but later never comes, so she feels ignored and their mother has to step in.

subtype: Approach: telling the younger one to wait forever [Pitfall]
passage: In the clinic waiting room, Mummy's phone was the only thing to play with, and Gagan had it. His little sister Lalremsiami leaned on his arm. "My turn?" "Later." She sat on her hands and watched the ceiling fan. Ten minutes. "Now?" "Later, I said. I'm on the last level." A new patient came in. The last level became another last level. Lalremsiami's lip began to shake. She walked across the room to their mother. "Gagan said later three times, and later never comes." Mummy took the phone, set it to show ten minutes, and handed it to Lalremsiami. "Then Gagan gets ten." Gagan slumped in his chair.

qa.q: What was the only thing to play with in the waiting room?
qa.a: Mummy's phone was the only thing to play with.

qa.q: How did Lalremsiami feel when "later" never came?
qa.a: She felt ignored and upset, with her lip beginning to shake.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it?
qa.a: "Later" had no fixed end, so it kept stretching; Gagan could have promised a turn when the current level ended, or set a timer himself.

qa.q: How does the waiting room scene look to Mummy?
qa.a: Mummy sees a little girl upset and an older child not sharing, so she has to step in and set the turns herself.

grounding: It shows an elder brother telling his little sister she can have a turn later, never giving it, and their mother having to step in.

subtype: Approach: telling the younger one to wait forever [Pitfall]
passage: I stay next door, and I see Charan and his little sister Nikita most evenings on the shared balcony. There's one cycle between them, a small red one. On Monday I heard Nikita ask for a turn. Charan said, "Later." I watched him ride circles for half an hour. "Later," again, when she asked a second time. By Wednesday she had stopped asking and just sat by the door, drawing with her finger in the dust on the floor. On Thursday she went inside and I heard her talking to their mother, her voice wobbly. Their mother came out, took the cycle and gave it to Nikita. Charan went in without a word. I don't know what he thought, but he didn't ride that evening.

qa.q: What colour is the cycle the siblings share?
qa.a: It is a small red one.

qa.q: What might Nikita have been feeling on Wednesday when she stopped asking?
qa.a: She may have felt left out and hopeless about ever getting a turn, though the neighbour can only guess from her sitting quietly.

qa.q: What would you advise Charan, and why?
qa.a: Give Nikita a clear turn after a fixed number of rounds, because a promise with no end feels like a no to a little sister.

qa.q: How might the week look to Charan and Nikita's mother?
qa.a: She has to step in to fix a problem that a fair turn could have avoided, and is probably disappointed in how Charan handled it.

grounding: It shows an elder brother who keeps saying later, a little sister who feels ignored and complains, and a mother who steps in.
